SECRETARY RUBIO: Even though they are radicals, there are people in the Iranian system that weigh the costs and benefits behind a decision.

It’s been two months since the state-imposed internet blackout began in Iran


NetBlocks (@netblocks)

🗓️ Exactly two months ago on 28 February, #Iran was thrown into digital darkness as authorities cut off access to the global internet.

Metrics show the blackout is now entering its 60th day after 1416 hours despite regime efforts to introduce tiered access for privileged groups.





— https://nitter.net/netblocks/status/2049024900187205780#m

This has been ongoing for some time now, but it's thanks to pushback by young Iranian women and girls who refused to abide by mandatory hijab rules after the 2022 Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. Authorities got overwhelmed by the numbers, and now it's out of their hands...


AFP News Agency (@AFP)

Images of women in Tehran not wearing headscarves, in apparent defiance of the Islamic republic's strict dress rule, have stirred interest outside Iran -- but for some it is no breakthrough.
